Compared with the Hereafter, this world is like what clings to a finger dipped in the ocean.
People will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, too troubled to look at one another; Abraham is clothed first, and some of the Prophet's companions are taken to the left.
People will be gathered in three groups, and with the sun a mile away they will stand in sweat according to deeds, up to knees, waists, mouths or ears.
The Prophet relays that Allah made His servants inclined to worship until Satan misled them, ordered him to fight Quraysh, and named three kinds in Paradise, five in Hell.
The dead are shown their seat morning and evening, the Prophet hears graves' torment, two angels question the buried, and two angels carry a believer's soul up.
The Prophet showed where each of Badr's dead would fall, then called to the Quraysh dead in the well, telling Umar they heard him but could not reply.
Whoever is thoroughly examined in the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is ruined; the easy reckoning in the verse is only the presentation of deeds.
Three days before his death the Prophet said that none should die except hoping only good from Allah.
Every servant will be raised in the state in which he dies, and when Allah punishes a people all are struck, then raised according to their deeds.
The Prophet warned of ruin for Arabia and that Gog and Magog's barrier had opened this much, saying people perish though good ones are among them when evil prevails.
An army sent against those seeking refuge at the House will sink into the earth on a plain, and those forced along will be raised by their intentions.
The Prophet saw turmoil falling among Medina's houses like rain; in coming turmoil sitting beats standing, so seek shelter, keep to one's flock or land, and blunt one's sword.
Two Muslims meeting with swords are both in the Fire; much bloodshed will precede the Hour, and Allah withheld the Prophet's request that his Ummah be spared killing one another.
Hudhaifa says the Prophet once described every turmoil to come before the Last Hour, some remembering and some forgetting, and Abu Zaid recalls a dawn-to-sunset address on past and future.
Hudhaifa tells Umar that a door, Umar himself, stands between him and the turmoil surging like waves and will be broken, and Jundub disputes with Hudhaifa over bloodshed at Jara'a.
Before the Hour the Euphrates will bare a gold mountain over which ninety-nine in a hundred die fighting, so take none; Iraq, Syria and Egypt will withhold coins and measures.
Before the Hour Romans will fight an army from Medina at Dabiq, whose victors take Constantinople before Jesus descends against the Dajjal, and the Romans will be the majority.
Before the Hour a war with Rome kills so many that spoils bring no joy, then news of the Dajjal comes; Arabia, Persia, Rome and the Dajjal will be conquered.
Ten signs precede the Hour: the smoke, the Dajjal, the beast, the sun rising in the west, Jesus's descent, Gog and Magog, three landslides and a fire driving people.
Before the Hour a fire from Hijaz will light camels' necks at Busra, Medina's dwellings will reach Ihab, and famine will come despite heavy rain as nothing grows.
Facing the east, the Prophet said turmoil would appear from there, where the horns of Satan rise; Salim reproached Iraqis for asking about minor sins while committing major ones.
Before the Hour, Daus women will circle Dhi al-Khalasa and Lat and Uzza be worshipped; a fragrant wind will take all with faith, the rest reverting to their forefathers' religion.
A man passing a grave will wish to be in it from calamity, and amid general bloodshed killer and slain will not know why, both in the Fire.
An Abyssinian with two small shanks will destroy the Ka'ba; before the Hour a man of Qahtan will drive people with his stick, and al-Jahjah will take the throne.
Before the Hour Muslims will fight peoples wearing hair shoes, with faces like hammered shields, small eyes, snub noses and red complexions, named in one report as the Turks.
Jabir said non-Arabs and Romans may stop Iraq's and Syria's food and money, and the Prophet said a caliph of the last age will give out wealth uncounted.
The Prophet told Ammar, digging the ditch, that rebels would kill him, and said this Quraish tribe would kill people of his Ummah, who had best keep apart from them.
Kisra and Caesar will die with no Kisra or Caesar after them, and the believers will spend their treasures in the cause of Allah.
These entries have no text in the source; they are kept with the report before them that Kisra and Caesar will die and their treasures be spent for Allah.
The Prophet tested Ibn Sayyad and kept Umar from killing him; Ibn Sayyad argued he was not the Dajjal, Paradise's earth was likened to musk, and Umar swore he was.
The Prophet tried to overhear Ibn Sayyad and warned the Dajjal is one-eyed, unlike Allah, with Kafir between his eyes; Hafsa told Ibn Umar anger would bring the Dajjal out.
Allah is not one-eyed, but the Dajjal is blind in the right eye, like a floating grape; every prophet warned of him, and Kafir is written between his eyes.
The Dajjal brings water and fire, or Paradise and Hell, each really the other, so whoever meets him should drink from what looks like fire; Noah too warned of him.
The Dajjal commands rain and treasures until Jesus kills him at Ludd; Gog and Magog swarm and perish, the earth is blessed, and a wind takes every Muslim.
The Dajjal kills and revives a believer who exposes him but cannot kill him again; the Prophet told Mughira he is insignificant to Allah despite his food and water.
Jesus kills the Dajjal; after seven peaceful years a cold wind takes all with faith, Satan leads the wicked to idols, and the trumpets raise people for judgement.
Abdullah b. Amr remembered that the first signs are the sun rising in the west and the beast appearing in the forenoon, the second following soon after the first.
From the pulpit the Prophet retold Tamim Dari's account of the chained Dajjal on an island, who would roam every land but Mecca and Medina, confirming his own words.
The Dajjal will cover every land but Mecca and Medina, whose passes angels guard; Medina will shake out its disbelievers and hypocrites, and seventy thousand Jews of Isfahan follow him.
People will flee from the Dajjal to the mountains, when the Arabs will be few, and no creation from Adam to the Hour is a greater trouble than he.
